name: Thomas pulse (Cnp patent table at 3 ms, both sides, 30 min)
origin: Alex W. Thomas and Michael A. Persinger (Lawson Health Research Institute / Laurentian University); the patent table (US 6,234,953: Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers, Persinger) as replayed in Persinger's lab
summary: The decelerating 'Thomas pulse' as Persinger's lab replayed it: the first 849 values of Table 1 of US patent 6,234,953 at 3 ms per point, one 2.55-s burst of 18 double-peaked pulses that slow down, repeated almost without a pause, for 30 min. In the lab's sensed-presence protocol (Saroka & Persinger 2013) this pattern ran for 30 min with a 10% right bias before 30 min of burst-firing.
notes: The patent prints 900 values in Table 1, the last 51 zeros. The lab's file 'contains 849 values between 0 and 255', played with 3-ms points and 3 ms between repeats (Persinger 2000 p.3 [661]); other lab texts print 837, 839, 859 or 890 points. The lab's helmet drove one left-right pair of its four at a time for 0.5 s, and in the sensed-presence protocol the pattern ran 30 min 'with a slight 10% increase over the right hemisphere' (Saroka & Persinger 2013 p.4-5 [398-399]). This program plays the 849 table values with 3-ms points and a 3-ms pause, the left side at 0.9 of the right. At this speed each 84-ms pulse has two positive peaks (24 per second at the start) and the last pulses come 201 ms apart: the lab's '25 Hz to 6 Hz' (Persinger 2000 p.3 [661]). The patent gives no point duration: its FIG. 1 ends at about 850 ms, which means 1 ms per point, with a peak of 100 uT (US 6,234,953 p.2, p.36); see lowfield-cnp-thomas-pulse. One left-right pair is on at a time (0.5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: 1 to 5 uT inside the helmet (Saroka & Persinger 2013 p.4 [398]); 5 uT at the right scalp in the 2000 case (Persinger 2000 p.3 [661]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Single-lab work. persinger-saroka-2015-sensed-presence runs the whole two-phase protocol. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). In the lab's epileptic rats the 3-ms setting provoked the most seizures (Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, fear or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes closed or opaque goggles, in a dark, quiet room (the lab used a shielded acoustic chamber).
schedule: One 30-min session. In the lab's protocol a break of about 5 min for a questionnaire and then 30 min of burst-firing follow (persinger-saroka-2015-sensed-presence).
source: Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 and FIG. 2 "Thomas Pulse (Cnp)" https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4):e0124136 (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s per cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Murugan 2013, MSc thesis, Laurentian University (849 points for the Thomas pulse at 3 ms, 3 ms between repeats; 248 points for burst-x) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/39c9c1ad-70ba-458d-a819-d24c20da217a ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, p. 89 (230-point burst-firing file, 3-ms points; Thomas file with 3-ms points and intervals) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Saroka 2015, doctoral thesis, Laurentian University, p. 29 (sensed-presence protocol: 30 min bilateral temporo-parietal frequency-modulated Thomas pattern, then 30 min BurstX) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/5260328f-a7c5-4d7b-b8a2-00b943eee977 ; Dixon & Persinger 2001, Int J Neurosci 108:87 (837 values at 1 ms once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11328704/ ; Tiller & Persinger 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:26 (forward vs reversed 3-ms Thomas pattern) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11883572/ ; Persinger & Belanger-Chellew 1999 (3-ms points and intervals, limbic-epileptic rats) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10597585/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
